decisions.reason: Because it directly builds on the firm's existing email delivery knowledge and has home-page prominence, the firm can readily assimilate early feedback and improve it, so it is likely kept.

Because document capture and recognition requires OCR and image-analysis knowledge outside the firm's email/fax core, the firm cannot easily interpret and learn from early results, so it is likely dropped.
Because email-to-fax conversion lies at the intersection of the firm's existing email and fax capabilities, the firm can rely on related knowledge to evaluate and refine it, so it is likely kept.
Because fax delivery optimization extends the firm's existing fax infrastructure knowledge, the firm can assimilate performance data and improve the feature, so it is likely kept.

Because email sandboxing requires specialised security knowledge beyond the firm's core email operations, the firm is less able to learn from early threat data and improve the product, so it is likely dropped.

Because multi-engine virus scanning demands antivirus and malware research expertise unrelated to the firm's existing email/fax knowledge, the firm cannot easily interpret detection results and enhance it, so it is likely dropped.
